$schema-comment: Anti-pattern phrases (LLM token optimization guide § 6) that should NEVER appear in the rendered prompt. Catches regression where polite filler creeps back in. The 'i' flag lets the patterns be case-insensitive — filler doesn't care about capitalization.

entries.why: Pure filler per the guide. The imperative form ('Make sure to' or just direct statement) is shorter and equally clear.
Filler — the instruction itself is the request.
Filler — just state the rule directly.

Output-side conversational wrapping that doesn't belong in instructions.

entries.pattern: I think it would be a good idea to
entries.why: Filler — the instruction itself is the request; never wrap in opinion.

entries.pattern: a command you ran \+ its observed output
entries.why: SPEC 2.0 §4.7 bans reviewer execution unconditionally (clud-bug#264/#260) — a `reproduction` is a CI check the forge already ran, never a command the reviewer executes itself. Locks the deleted executable-probe framing out of the prompt (the negated form, 'never a command you ran', is the correct replacement and legitimately appears).
